newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: PRESS DIGEST-Australian Sports News - June 30.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST-Australian Sports News - June 30.

text.p: (Compiled for Reuters by Media Monitors)
THE AUSTRALIAN

Australian Olympic Swimmer Kieren Perkins led an Australian assault at the Santa Carla international swim meet yesterday. Perkin's claimed victory in the 400m freestyle, while Jason Samuelson, Michael Klim and Samantha Riley also won their races. Page 27.

The Sydney Swans won over the reigning premiers North Melbourne in the Australian Football League at the Sydney Cricket Ground yesterday. A finals game and a top four finish is likely for the Swans, whose captain Paul Kelly played his 150th game. Page 29

The Australian rowing team won seven gold medals, two silver, and four bronze at the Mass Holland Beker Regatta in Amsterdam on Saturday. The unbeaten men's eight and men's lightweight eight won gold medals in Paris last weekend at the World Cup. Page 30
THE SYDNEY MORNING HERALD

In the National Basketball League on Saturday night the South East Melbourne Magic defeated the Sydney Kings 127-100. Kings coach Alan Black says the Magic are the best team in the league and are simply to good. The Magic are tipped to win their second staight championship.

Australia's 3-0 win over New Zealand on Saturday afternoon in the Oceania World Cup soccer play-offs proved the ability of Australia's home-based players. Amidst pre-match discussions centring on the unbalanced experience of the opposing teams, it was thethree home-based Australians that excelled themselves.

The Australian Wallabies rugby team may be without two of their most experienced backs next weekend in their game against New Zealand in the first encounter of the Bledisloe Cup. Matthew Bourke may miss the game due to groin complaint and Jason Little maybe forced out due to hip muscle injury.
THE AGE

Australian football team Hawthorn won over Melbourne by an amazing 63 points at Waverley Park yesterday. The Demons made off-field headlines last week as Joesph Gutnick was seen to have tempted Essendon player Danny Corcoran with an offer too good to refuse. Page 11.

Rain interrupted golfer Greg Norman's third-round performance in the A$2 million St Jude Classic in Memphis. Norman was nine under and four strokes off the pace, while fellow Australian Craig Parry was seven under after eight holes. Page 19.

Australian high jumper Tim Forsyth and hurdler Rohan Robinson finished well in a championship in Zagreb last Friday. Forsyth won the high jump with his first effort of 2.30m, while Robinson came second in the 400m hurdles. Page 19.
THE HERALD SUN

Basketball team the Canberra Cannons won over the Melbourne Tigers last night 92-82, shaking the Tigers' confidence following their win over Newcastle on Saturday night. Cannons coach Brett Flanigan told his team to take advantage of the Tigers' fatigue and it was evident they did. Page 87.

In the National Netball League yesterday, Melbourne Phoenix celebrated a 24 goal victory over the Perth Orioles. The Orioles are feeling the pressure as it broke their three-game winning streak and dislodged them from the top four. Page 94.

Australian Motorbike rider Michael Doohan won his sixth win in seven races at the Dutch Grand Prix in Assen on the weekend. Doolan leads the 500cc world championship by 68 points with eight races remaining but says he is not over the finish line yet. Page90.
THE DAILY TELEGRAPH

The two new clubs in Super League, Hunter and Adelaide, once ranked as outsiders, are now in contention for one of the five final spots. The remaining five rounds will see eight teams battle for a spot in the finale to the Telstra Cup. Page 45.

A life sized bronze sculpture of champion winning racehorse Octagonal will be erected for display at Woodlands Stud. Jack and Bob Ingram borrowed the idea from Ireland's Coolmore Stud where two champion racehorse statues are displayed on the property. Pag 50.

Australian tennis player Mark Woodforde won 5-7 5-7 6-2 6-4 6-1 against Briton Chris Wilkinson at Wimbledon on Saturday. Woodforde, 32, says he relied on his years of experience to defeat Wilkinson who after winning the first two sets couldn't maintain the standard for the remaining three. Page 38.
-- Sydney Newsroom 61-2 9373-1800
